one_line_description.value: Podio is a work management platform with no-code tools, flexible workflows, and customizable business solutions.
one_line_description.quote: Unify and automate work with no-code tools, flexible workflows and customizable business solutions.

has_public_api.quote: The Podio API is a complete programmable interface to all Podio functionality.

api_breadth.value: ~40 functional API areas covering applications, items, tasks, files, hooks, users, search, etc.; read-write
api_breadth.quote: Our API is split up into different areas, that each contains a subset of methods grouped by functionality.

auth_methods.quote: The Podio API uses the OAuth2 protocol for authentication.

oauth_scopes_documented.quote: See Scopes & Permissions for details about the value of GRANTED_SCOPE_STRING

access_model.quote: You just have to sign in or sign up with Podio, and go to the API key tab in your settings.

access_notes.value: Self-serve: sign in or sign up and generate an API key from account settings. Production/high-volume usage may require a paid API Add-on for higher rate limits. The official client libraries page notes Citrix does not maintain the libraries.
access_notes.quote: It's easy to get one or more API keys for accessing your Podio data.

rate_limits.value: 1,000 calls/hour (Limit B, standard); 250 calls/hour (Limit A, resource-intensive); per user per API key on a rolling hour; HTTP 420 returned when exceeded
rate_limits.quote: The general limit is 1,000 API calls per hour, but if the API call is deemed resource-intensive, a lower rate of 250 calls per hour is enforced.

webhooks.quote: Hooks are webhooks that can call external sites when certain actions occur in Podio.

sdk_languages.quote: We currently provide wrappers for PHP, .NET, Ruby, Java, Python, Android and Objective-C which make working with common API operations very simple.

verdict_reason: Podio exposes a broad, documented API covering the entire product, with docs split into roughly 40 functional areas. A developer can sign up and generate an API key from account settings without sales contact, and authentication is OAuth2. Rate limits are modest but documented (250/1,000 calls per hour) and can be raised via a paid API Add-on.
open_questions: API type (REST/JSON) is stated on developers.podio.com/index/api, which appeared in search results but was not included in SOURCES text; confirm before finalizing api_type.

A community repo (github.com/phases/mcp-server-for-podio) appeared in search results but was not fetched or verified; community_mcp_servers left not_found.
No source documents a dedicated sandbox/test environment; tutorials only mention installing an app into a 'test space'.
No source documents an API versioning, deprecation, or sunset policy.
The client libraries page notes Citrix does not maintain these libraries and also lists a JavaScript library not covered by the cited quote; confirm current official SDK status.
Confirm whether free Podio accounts have full API access: a FAQ search snippet suggested both paid and free accounts have full API access, but the FAQ page text was not included in SOURCES.
Podio uses HTTP 420 for rate-limit errors, which is non-standard; confirm in production.
